title: GeometryReading
description:
A generated reading of the shipped artefact's geometry.

A ledger under VDS S-4(2): generated, never hand-edited, and byte-reproducible by the named command. It is an INPUT to the proof and never a record of it.

contentDigest.description:
A digest over every OTHER field of this reading.

# Why the proof is worthless without it

`geometry` reads this file as its ONLY measurement. Without a digest, a bound that is being exceeded can be brought back inside it by editing one integer in a YAML file, and the proof flips from failed to passed with no surface having changed and nothing anywhere reporting it. That is the defect VDS exists to catch, and the twelfth kind shipped with it: the first eleven ledgers all carry a digest and this one did not.

It is not a security control and does not pretend to be one. An author who edits the reading can recompute the digest in the same act, exactly as VDS S-8(5) records for the enforcement lock. What it removes is the SILENT edit: a number changed by hand and left, which is the realistic failure and the one that leaves no trace.

`taken_at` is INSIDE the digest, unlike `generated_at` on the figma ledger. There the timestamp is metadata and excluding it keeps a re-pull of an unchanged file from moving a digest a proof cites. Here it is EVIDENCE: R3 measures the bound's window from it, so moving it changes what the proof concludes, and a digest that did not cover it would leave the one field with the most leverage unwitnessed.

doesNotCover.description:
What the reader knows it did not cover, in the reader's own words.

Required to be stated, because a census that does not publish its own blind spots reads as complete.

generatedBy.description: The command that reproduces this file byte for byte.

sources.description: The artefacts actually read, repository-relative. Named so a reader can tell a reading of the built bundle from a reading of one stylesheet that happens to sit beside it.

takenAt.description: When the reading was taken. The proof measures the bound's DIRECTION against this moment and never against the wall clock: a rule read from the system time would make a proof's findings change without any input changing, and VDS S-7(2)(1) requires an unchanged check to cite the same evidence.

considered.description: Every surface the reader looked at, of this kind.

nonCompliant.description: Of those, how many do not comply.

sample.description: Where the worst offenders are, so a row is a job somebody can pick up. Repository-relative, and a sample rather than the full list: a ledger carrying six hundred paths is a ledger nobody reads.

undecided.description: Of those, how many the reader could not resolve.

ReadFrom.description:
What a reading was taken FROM.

VDS S-7A(4): geometry is read from the SHIPPED artefact, never from a model of it. A code model of the intended design is a legitimate design tool and is NOT admissible as the subject of this proof, because it is a third artefact that drifts: on the subscriber project a 17-page code model of the design drifted so completely that it came to model the OUTGOING system it was built to replace.

# Why [`ReadFrom::CodeModel`] is representable at all

It would be stronger, on the face of it, to leave it out of the enum so a code-model reading could not be written down. It is weaker. A generator that read a code model would then have no way to say so truthfully, and its only route to a parseable ledger would be to label the reading `ShippedSource`. The variant exists so that the honest recorder produces a finding that NAMES the problem, rather than a validation error that teaches mislabelling. The proof refuses it; the type does not hide it.

oneOf.description: The stylesheet that ships: the built, compiled CSS a browser receives. The strongest reading, because it is what the user's machine renders.

The source that compiles into what ships. Admissible: it is the shipping code, not a description of it. Weaker than the stylesheet by exactly the distance a build step can introduce, and a reading must say which it took so nobody has to guess.
A hand-authored model of the intended design. REFUSED by the proof (S-7A(4)). Representable so it can be refused by name.

A reading of the DESIGN FILE - the Figma file that is the system of record for what was decided ([2026] VJS-CC-OPBOX 3 D1). Admitted by [2026] VJS-CC-VIBE-DESIGN-SYSTEM 3 and NOT shipped: no browser renders it, so it is refused as the subject of the shipped bound for its OWN reason - a different subject, not an unreliable one - never under code_model's. Any output derived from one must name the drawing as its subject; a number that does not name its subject is two numbers wearing one name.

SurfaceKind.description:
The shapes a bound may be declared over. CLOSED, and closed on purpose.

VDS S-7A(3): the bound is per SURFACE KIND and never one number for the estate. The subscriber project's instrument reported "561 hand-rolled card-geometry containers, pin 561", and that number names no work: it cannot be assigned to anybody, it cannot be finished, and it hides which shapes are worst. An enum rather than a free string is the strongest available form of that rule, because one undifferentiated bucket is then unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.

oneOf.description: The weight of a surface's boundary: a border, a ring, a divider.
Control density: the spacing step a surface sets its own padding and gaps from.
Type scale: the size and leading step a surface sets its text from.

Timestamp.description: UTC, second resolution, trailing Z. The one canonical form VDS writes.
